content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It type-checks, matches the original on every input I tried, and cuts the bundle from 9012 to 639 bytes gzipped.

| | Original (`src/module.ts`) | Migrated (`out/module.ts`) |
|---|---|---|
| Bundle size (min+gzip) | 9012 bytes | 639 bytes |
| Own code in bundle | 177 bytes | 95 bytes |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.json` | — | passes |

The migrated file uses three es-toolkit 1.53.2 imports:

- **`doubled`**: `mapValues` from `es-toolkit/object`, unchanged apart from the import.
- **`byNameKey`**: `keyBy` from `es-toolkit/array`, with a one-line adapter `(row) => row.name`. The es-toolkit version takes a key function, not a property name.
- **`isBlank`**: `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat/isEmpty`, a default import. es-toolkit has no non-compat `isEmpty`. `isEmptyObject` exists, but it returns false for arrays, so it does not match lodash.

I kept the exported names, signatures, and the `Row` and `Config` types. The lodash imports are gone, and nothing was installed.

For the bundle-size goal, I compared the adapter route with using `es-toolkit/compat/keyBy` with the string `'name'` directly. That variant measured 3386 bytes gzipped, so I kept the adapter. I did not try other alternatives.

To check behaviour, I bundled the original and migrated modules and compared them on the example inputs plus 11,019 randomized checks across the three input ranges. Results and key order matched in every case. Scratch files are in the scratchpad, not in the project. `src/module.ts` is unchanged, and `out/` contains only `module.ts`.
